description: Generated from phase package manifests, detected audio assets, and benchmark-authored audio provenance.

audio.strategy: Live synthesis only. One piano-like voice is computed sample by sample by a TypeScript DSP kernel (additive synthesis: a bank of exponentially decaying sine partials per note). The kernel runs in an AudioWorklet; if the worklet cannot load, the same kernel runs in a ScriptProcessorNode and the status reads 'Fallback'. No recorded samples are bundled, fetched, or played, and no audio buffers are generated or stored.

generatedSources.name: Basic Piano partial bank
generatedSources.description: Per note: up to 32 sine partials at stretched (inharmonic) frequencies, amplitudes shaped by strike position and a velocity-dependent spectral slope and felt lowpass, each decaying exponentially with higher partials decaying faster; the lowest 6 partials also carry a slower, 0.9-cent-sharp aftersound component for two-stage decay and beating. Attack ramp of 1-4 ms, pitch-dependent damper release, mild note-dependent stereo pan.
generatedSources.license: Original code written for this candidate; no third-party audio or DSP code.

generatedSources.name: Hammer noise burst
generatedSources.description: A 12 ms decaying burst of lowpassed pseudo-random noise per strike, generated per sample by a xorshift32 generator seeded from the note number and strike order (deterministic). It is computed live; it is not a noise buffer.
generatedSources.license: Original code written for this candidate.

notes: There are zero audio files in this candidate: no .wav, .mp3, .ogg, .flac, or encoded sample data of any kind.

The voice is a synthesized approximation of a piano. It is described as synthesis in the UI ('synthesized piano voice (live additive synthesis, not a recording)') and is never presented as a recording or as a Nord piano model.
Recorded Grand / Upright / Electric sample sets required by specs/nord-stage-4.piano.json are Phase 2 scope and are not present.

Signal path: voices -> sum -> master gain (fixed 0.7 in Phase 1) -> soft limiter -> one output node -> AudioContext.destination. There is exactly one connection to the destination and nothing bypasses the master stage.
Polyphony is 32 voices with deterministic stealing: released voices first, then pedal-held, then held keys; oldest strike first within a class.
The panel's Master Level knob is decorative in Phase 1 and is not connected to the master gain.

audio.strategy: One AudioContext and one output node. A TypeScript DSP kernel (src/audio/dsp/stage.ts) runs in an AudioWorklet, or in a ScriptProcessorNode when the worklet is unavailable. Grand, Upright, and Electric play bundled recordings (198 FLAC files, 12 MB, decoded by the app's own FLAC decoder). Clav, Digital, and Misc are live additive synthesis and are labelled as synthesis in the model name, on the Program display, and in the status console. If a sample set cannot be loaded, its layer plays a synthesized stand-in voice labelled "Fallback Synth Piano", the type LED flashes, and the audio status reads Fallback, never Ready. All effects are computed live in the kernel; no impulse responses or other audio buffers are bundled or generated.

notes: Signal path, per Piano layer: voices -> Piano Timbre EQ -> Mod 1 -> Mod 2 -> Delay -> Amp Sim/EQ (or LP24/HP24 filter) -> Compressor -> Reverb -> Rotary (when routed) -> layer level; then both layers -> sum -> master gain (Master Level) -> soft limiter -> one output node -> AudioContext.destination. There is exactly one connection to the destination and nothing bypasses the master stage.

The Rotary has one shared rotor (speed, acceleration, angles, drive setting). Each routed layer passes through its own crossover and delay lines driven by that rotor, so that the layer level can follow the Rotary as the documented order requires; two routed layers therefore overdrive separately rather than as a sum.

Group and Global are implemented as shared settings: an edit is applied to every chain in the group (or to every chain for a Global unit), and entering the mode copies the focused chain's settings to the others. Each layer still runs its own instance of the unit, before its level fader; a Global Reverb is not moved after the Rotary (the effects spec excludes that nuance).
Polyphony is 48 voices per layer (a Unison note uses 2 or 3) with deterministic stealing: released voices first, then pedal-held, then held keys; oldest strike first within a class.

Velocity response: loudness follows velocity^1.7 after the KB Touch curve; Dyn Comp reduces that exponent. Within one velocity layer the softer end is slightly lowpassed so adjacent layers meet smoothly.
The app decodes FLAC itself (src/audio/library/flac.ts) instead of calling decodeAudioData, so the same bytes give the same samples in every browser and in the tests.

Sample files are fetched by relative path from the build output (public/samples -> dist/samples). No network host is contacted. Opening dist/index.html from file:// blocks both the worklet and the sample fetches in most browsers; the app then says so and plays the labelled fallback, or reports that it is silent.

generatedSources.name: Synth oscillators
generatedSources.usedBy: Synth layers A, B, and C (Analog mode; there is no Samples mode).
generatedSources.description: Fourteen waveforms in five categories, each a different algorithm. Pure: sine, triangle, polyBLEP saw, square, 33 % and 10 % pulse, white noise (Osc Ctrl has no effect). Sync: a saw or square slave hard-synced to the note, with band-limited corrections at the slave wraps and at the reset (Osc Ctrl raises the slave pitch up to three octaves). Multi: three stacked saws, mono (Osc Ctrl detunes them up to 50 cents). Super: seven saws or five squares spread in pitch and across the stereo field (Osc Ctrl is spread and width). FM-H: two sine operators at 1:1 (Osc Ctrl is the modulation index, 0 to 9).
generatedSources.license: Original code written for this candidate; no third-party audio or DSP code.

generatedSources.usedBy: Synth layers A, B, and C.
generatedSources.description: A topology-preserving state-variable filter per voice (LP12, LP24 as two cascaded stages, HP, BP) with keyboard tracking, resonance, and a tanh drive stage in front; attack/decay/release envelopes for oscillator, filter, and amplifier (decay at maximum is sustain); one LFO per layer (triangle, saw down, saw up, square, sample & hold) to pitch, Osc Ctrl, or filter; poly, mono, and legato with last/low/high priority and constant-rate glide; unison as two to four detuned, panned copies inside one voice; vibrato (On, Delay, Wheel, Pedal); and an arpeggiator / gate that counts samples inside the kernel, so its steps are sample-exact and repeatable.

notes: Phase 3 signal graph: six buses — Piano A, Piano B, Organ, Synth A, Synth B, Synth C — each with its own chain (Mod 1, Mod 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ or filter, Compressor, Reverb), its own path through the one shared rotor when routed, and its level; they sum into the one master gain and soft limiter and leave through the one output node. The two Organ layers share the Organ bus, so their level faders are applied before the shared chain. There is still exactly one AudioContext and one connection to its destination.

Keys reach a layer only inside its keyboard zones, scaled across a split crossfade (a linear gain that is 0.5 at the split point), and with the program transpose added; all of that happens inside the kernel, in src/audio/dsp/stage.ts.

The Organ is routed to the Rotary by its own button in the Rotary Speaker group, independently of Layer Effects On (it is the speaker, not a layer effect). It reaches the rotary amplifier 12 dB hotter than its bus level so that Drive overdrives it; the level is restored after the rotary.

Master Clock: the tempo is program state. A synced Synth LFO, arpeggiator, Delay, or Mod 1 has its rate derived from the tempo and the subdivision its knob selects (1/2, 1/4, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T) when the sound state is derived; the kernel receives plain rates in Hz. Keyboard Sync restarts a synced layer when a key is played after all keys were up.
